featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a true food lover, Noor Mohammadi Hotel is nothing short of heaven. I finally got to try their legendary Nalli Nihari, and honestly… it lives up to every bit of the hype.

The nihari was rich, slow-cooked to perfection, with the marrow melting into the gravy, bursting with deep, soulful flavors. Every spoon felt warm, comforting, and indulgent — the kind of dish that makes you pause and appreciate good food.

And just when I thought it couldn’t get better, the meal ended with their Rabdi. Thick, creamy, and perfectly balanced in sweetness, it was the ideal dessert to round off such a hearty feast. You can actually taste the patience and tradition in every bite.
No fancy plating, no unnecessary drama — just authentic, old-school flavors that hit straight to the heart. Noor Mohammadi doesn’t just serve food; it serves heritage on a plate.

featured_reviews.name: Shaikh Kadir
featured_reviews.review_text:
This place truly gave me a heartwarming experience and the kind of food that reminds you what real, honest cooking tastes like. It’s amazing to know that this restaurant has been around for over 102 years, carrying forward a legacy of authentic flavors and consistent quality. You can really feel that heritage in every dish they serve.

The food was absolutely delicious and clearly made with care and good-quality ingredients. I loved how every bite had that traditional touch — nothing fancy, just pure, flavorful food made right. My personal favorites were the Mutton Sanju Baba and the Haleem. The mutton was soft, juicy, and full of flavor, while the haleem was rich, creamy, and perfectly spiced — the kind that instantly makes you smile after the first spoonful.

The ambiance adds to the experience — simple, calm, and full of character. It feels like a place where stories have been shared for generations. The staff was really friendly and attentive, making sure we were comfortable and enjoying our food.

Overall, I’d say this isn’t just a restaurant it’s a part of culinary history. If you love traditional, soulful food that warms both your heart and your stomach, this place is a must-visit.

featured_reviews.name: Moumita Roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Noor Mohammadi Hotel and it was a truly memorable experience for anyone who loves authentic Mughlai food. This place is quite iconic and well-known for its rich, flavorful dishes.

The highlight, of course, is their legendary chicken dishes—especially the Chicken Sanju Baba, which is packed with bold spices and has a rich, indulgent taste. The food overall is delicious, with generous portions and that proper old-school Mumbai Mughlai flavor.

The ambience is simple and no-frills, but that’s part of its charm. It’s more about the food than the setting. The place is usually quite crowded, and you might have to wait a bit for a table, especially during peak hours.

Service is quick considering the rush, though it can feel a bit hectic at times. Hygiene and seating are decent but not luxurious, so it’s best to go in with the right expectations.

Overall, Noor Mohammadi is a must-visit if you’re looking to enjoy authentic, hearty Mughlai cuisine in Mumbai. It’s not about fine dining, but about great taste and a truly local food experience.

featured_reviews.name: Faiz F
featured_reviews.review_text:
Once a legendary staple of Mumbai’s culinary scene since 1958, Gulshan-e-Iran appears to have lost the magic that built its heritage. The shift away from their famous buff seekh has left a noticeable void in the menu that the chicken alternatives simply cannot fill. A recent attempt at the Chicken Seekh Kabab and Tawa Paratha proved to be a major disappointment, lacking the flavor profile one expects from such an established name. While the Chicken Kheema in Green Masala offers a saving grace with its well-balanced, mild spices, the overall lack of variety in the tawa and grill sections forced a pivot to basic Dal Rice just to round out the meal.

Ultimately, this iconic spot now functions better as an emergency food option rather than a dining destination. Given its location in a high-traffic business market with limited surrounding choices, it serves its purpose for a quick, functional bite, but it no longer carries the "must-visit" status of its glory days. For those seeking a more satisfying meal in the area, Patel Restaurant stands out as the superior recommendation.

featured_reviews.name: Janhavi Raut
featured_reviews.review_text:
Kyani & Co. is a classic Iranian café serving authentic Iranian cuisine. The place is always crowded, and you’ll notice a good mix of locals and foreigners, which shows how popular and well-known it is.

Coming to the food, their chicken dishes stood out. The Chicken Cheese Kebab was actually very nice—it was stuffed with cheese from inside and had a hot-dog–like shape. It felt filling and had a good amount of chicken, which I liked the most.

I also tried the chicken samosa, but I felt the chicken quantity was a bit less, with more masala in the filling. Similarly, the mutton cutlet had more potato than mutton. Personally, I prefer meat-forward dishes.

The ambience is really great with an old-world charm, but photography is not allowed inside. I clicked one photo and was asked not to take pictures, which was a bit disappointing considering how beautiful the place is.

Overall, it’s an authentic Iranian café with a lovely atmosphere. The food is good, especially the chicken items, though the filling ratios may not suit everyone’s taste.

Visited Kyani & Co. and honestly, it felt less like a café visit and more like a journey back in time. The moment you walk in, the old-world charm hits you — vintage wooden furniture, classic tiled floors, and an atmosphere that carries stories from over 100 years ago. It’s raw, real, and beautifully untouched.
We ordered the iconic Irani chai, bun maska, and kheema pav — and every bite was pure nostalgia. The chai had that perfect strong, comforting flavor, the bun maska was soft with just the right amount of buttery goodness, and the kheema pav was rich, flavorful, and absolutely satisfying.
What makes this place special isn’t just the food — it’s the experience. No fancy frills, no modern distractions, just timeless simplicity done right.
A small heads-up: it’s strictly cash only — no cards, no UPI — which somehow adds to its old-school vibe.
If you’re in Mumbai and want to experience something authentic, soulful, and truly fascinating, this place is not just a café… it’s a legacy you can taste.

Firstly, I think this place hasn't been given justified reviews.. primarily because with the look, people take it as a place for LIG's to visit.
Well, I have visited enough places and exclusive South Indian ones from National Capital to all over South India..
Firstly, the hotel is 76 years old ! Yeah Circa 1953..
The layout and the marble settings you see inside is 41 years old..Yeah..they haven't changed it and trust me, it looks as good as new !
They take lot of pride in their job, making good and tasty food and feeding you..Rates are nominal for the service and for a place like 5mins in a cab from CST..
I had Butter Idli and Ghee Roast. It was very well made..as good as or better than many hifi vegetarian outlets..
If you want to a authentic..clean and good South Indian food with appreciable ambience.., you won't be disappointed..
And I said Authentic as the first expression because other places may fancy you with lights and space.. but they all tweek authenticity ! Rather quite tough to reach that spot..
So wonderful place.. Will definitely go and try some other dish next time..maybe over lunch..
They have an AC Family Room on Level 1..So, don't get discouraged with the lean trim space on Ground Floor alone..

featured_reviews.name: Stringzzz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya – A Timeless Taste of Authentic Gujarati Thali

Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya is one of the most iconic and beloved places to experience authentic Gujarati cuisine. Known for its traditional thali, warm hospitality, and consistent quality, this legendary eatery has earned a special place in the hearts of locals as well as visitors. Dining here feels less like eating at a restaurant and more like being welcomed into a Gujarati household.

The moment you enter Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya, you are greeted with simplicity and warmth. The interiors are modest, clean, and functional, reflecting the traditional values of Gujarati culture where food quality and hospitality matter more than luxury décor. The seating arrangement is organized, and despite the heavy rush during peak hours, the staff manages the crowd efficiently.

The highlight, without any doubt, is the Gujarati Thali. The thali is a wholesome and balanced meal that represents the true essence of Gujarat’s culinary heritage. It usually includes a variety of rotating dishes such as shaak (vegetable curries), kadhi, dal, rotli or puri, rice, khichdi, farsan, chutneys, pickles, and traditional sweets like shrikhand or mohanthal. Each item is freshly prepared and served hot.

One of the most impressive aspects of Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya is the unlimited serving system. The staff continuously serves food with great attentiveness, ensuring that guests never feel rushed or restricted. The flavors are authentic—mildly spiced, well-balanced, and comforting—making the food suitable for all age groups. The use of fresh ingredients and traditional cooking methods is clearly reflected in the taste.

Historically, Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya has been serving Gujarati food for decades and is considered a cultural landmark. It has preserved the original style of Gujarati dining, where meals are meant to nourish both the body and the soul. Many regular visitors associate the place with nostalgia, family gatherings, and cultural pride.

Cleanliness and hygiene are well maintained throughout the restaurant. Plates, serving areas, and dining spaces are kept tidy, even during peak hours. The staff is polite, disciplined, and well trained, adding to the overall pleasant dining experience.

The pricing is reasonable, especially considering the quality, quantity, and authenticity of the food served. It offers excellent value for money and is often recommended as a must-visit place for anyone wanting to experience true Gujarati cuisine.

Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya attracts a diverse crowd—families, elderly guests, tourists, and food lovers from across India. Despite the popularity and long waiting times during weekends, the management ensures smooth operations and quick table turnover without compromising service quality.

Overall, Shree Thaker Bhojnalaya is not just a restaurant but a celebration of Gujarati tradition, flavors, and hospitality. If you want to experience a soulful Gujarati thali prepared with authenticity and served with warmth, this place is an absolute must-visit. It leaves you with a satisfied heart, a happy stomach, and a deep appreciation for Gujarat’s rich culinary culture.

featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best culinary experiences I’ve had in Mumbai. I stumbled upon this spot tucked into one of the city’s busiest, most crowded streets, and it was absolutely worth navigating the chaos to get there.

I ordered the pav bhaji and chole bhature, and both were outstanding. The pav bhaji was rich, buttery, and perfectly spiced with that authentic street-style flavor, yet it felt clean and hygienic. The chole bhature was just as impressive — fluffy, hot bhature paired with chole that had deep, balanced masala without being overly oily. You could taste the freshness in every bite.

What really elevated the experience was the staff. I was new to Mumbai and a bit overwhelmed, but they were incredibly friendly and patient. They took the time to explain the menu, recommend what to try, and even shared how each dish is traditionally eaten. At no point did I feel rushed despite the constant crowd outside.

I also noticed how neat and well-maintained the place was. For a busy street-side eatery, the tables were clean, the serving area was organized, and the staff did not feel rushed.

Great food, warm service, and surprising neatness in the heart of Mumbai’s bustle. I’ll definitely be back. Highly recommended if you want authentic flavors without compromising on hygiene

featured_reviews.name: tushar alphonso
featured_reviews.review_text:
​Stepping into DELHI RASOI is an exercise in managing expectations. If you're looking for sprawling dining halls, endless menu pages, or a spot for a large, rowdy gathering, this isn't it. But if you're a vegetarian seeking a perfectly executed, intensely flavorful meal that bypasses quantity for sheer quality, you absolutely must find this little 💎 GEM
​The space is small and intimate. The tables are close, the movement is restricted, and during peak hours, the atmosphere can feel more bustling. It has a focused, cozy, and slightly chaotic energy that somehow feels authentic—you know the kitchen is working hard just feet away.
​The starter and main course sections are intentionally limited. This might initially feel restrictive, but it quickly becomes RASOI's superpower. Instead of spreading its focus on Quantity, Rasoi concentrates on Quality, perfecting a handful of dishes.
The flavor is where this restaurant shines, brilliantly exceeding its humble surroundings. We tried the "Cheese Corn Ball, Paneer Chilli, Mushroom Chilli, Cheese Paratha" to start, and they were crispy on the outside, tender inside, and packed with a fresh, vibrant kick that felt utterly homemade. For the main, "Paneer Lababdar, Baigaan Bharta, Tadka Kadi Pakoda with Butter & Ghee Phulkas" was a revelation—rich, creamy, and complex, clearly cooked with ingredients and balanced spices. Every dish we sampled was bursting with deep, memorable flavor, proving that the kitchen staff are true masters of their craft.
​The verdict:
DELHI RASOI is the ideal spot for a quick, exceptionally tasty lunch or an intimate dinner where the focus is solely on the plate. Come for the fantastic food, not the fancy décor or extensive options. Just be prepared to wait a little, if you arrive at a busy time, and know that every bite is worth the WAIT.
